skill.name: firecrawl-monitor
skill.description: Create Firecrawl monitors that watch pages, sites, or web search results and send change alerts by email or webhook.
skill.summary: Set up Firecrawl monitors for recurring page, site, and web-search change alerts.
skill.author: firecrawl

security_audit.summary: Static findings primarily matched Markdown backticks, example URLs, relative links, and natural-language schedules, so they were marked false positive. Two contextual risks remain: the allowed npx command can execute an unpinned npm package, and monitor notifications can send page diffs to external destinations. Publish with clear install and notification warnings, or tighten the allowed tools.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx execution is allowed by the skill metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a preinstalled, verified firecrawl CLI command, or pin the npx package version and document package verification steps.

remediation.issue: Webhook and email notifications can disclose monitored content.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for every destination and warn before monitoring private or sensitive pages.

remediation.issue: Static analysis misclassifies many Markdown examples as executable patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly fenced and label sample URLs, emails, and relative links as documentation placeholders.

content.value_statement: Teams need reliable alerts when pages, site content, or web search results change. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Firecrawl monitors with schedules, goals, and notification channels.
actual_capabilities: Create single-page monitors with natural-language schedules and goals.
Create batch URL monitors for several pages in one setup.
Create crawl-based monitors for recurring site-wide change checks.
Create web monitors that search for new matching results.
Configure webhook and email notifications for monitor events.
Inspect monitor checks, page status, snapshots, and field-level diffs.
limitations: Requires Firecrawl CLI access and a configured Firecrawl account.
Cannot monitor zero-data-retention teams according to the source instructions.
Web monitors alert on new search results, not changed or removed results.

use_cases.title: Track Competitor Pricing
use_cases.description: Monitor pricing pages and alert when plan names, prices, billing periods, limits, or features change.

use_cases.title: Monitor Documentation Changes
use_cases.description: Watch docs, changelogs, and status pages so teams can react when important content changes.

use_cases.title: Watch Market Signals
use_cases.description: Create web monitors for new launches, funding rounds, papers, releases, or brand mentions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Page Monitor
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one known URL.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Firecrawl monitor for [URL]. Alert me when [change] happens. Send notifications to [email or webhook].

prompt_templates.title: Monitor Several URLs
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up one Firecrawl monitor for these pages: [URLs]. Use this goal: [goal]. Run it every [interval].

prompt_templates.title: Create a Web Monitor
prompt_templates.scenario: Search-based monitoring when no fixed URL exists.
prompt_templates.prompt: Monitor the web for [topic]. Use focused search queries and alert only when results match [decision criteria].

prompt_templates.title: Build Structured Tracking
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Firecrawl monitor that extracts [fields] from [URL] and alerts when those fields change substantively.

output_examples.input: Monitor this pricing page for plan price changes.
output_examples.output: A monitor plan with an hourly schedule, a pricing-focused goal, and email or webhook delivery after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Alert me when new funding rounds mention our competitors.
output_examples.output: A web monitor setup with focused search queries, a goal that filters irrelevant news, and a seven-day search window.

output_examples.input: Show changes from the latest monitor check.
output_examples.output: A check summary grouped by changed, new, removed, and error pages with key field differences.

best_practices: Write goals that state the business trigger and any user-provided exclusions.
Use web monitors only when there is no known URL to watch.
Confirm webhook URLs and email recipients before creating monitors.
anti_patterns: Using a monitor for a one-time page read.
Adding broad search queries without a precise goal.
Sending alerts to external recipients without clear user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill monitor?
faq.answer: It monitors known URLs, groups of URLs, crawled sites, and search results for new or changed content.

faq.question: Does it require cron jobs?
faq.answer: No. Firecrawl handles scheduling, checks, diffing, and notification delivery server-side.

faq.question: Can it monitor the whole web?
faq.answer: Yes. Web monitors use search queries plus a goal to alert on new matching results.

faq.question: How does it reduce noisy alerts?
faq.answer: The goal tells the AI judge which content changes matter and which page churn to ignore.

faq.question: Can it send webhook alerts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can send monitor events to approved webhook destinations provided by the user.

faq.question: What should users provide before setup?
faq.answer: Users should provide a URL or search queries, a schedule, a goal, and an approved notification destination.
